chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man accuses his wife before he consummates the marriage with her.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is given the Hadd (punishment), and separation is effected between him and her.'

key_terms.يُخَلَّى بَيْنَهُ وَ بَيْنَهَا: Separation is effected between him and her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man accuses his wife before consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a husband who accuses his wife of zina before consummation (dakhul) is subject to the Hadd punishment for slander (qadhf) and the marriage is dissolved. This ruling highlights the distinction between pre-consummation and post-consummation scenarios in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing the severity of false accusation even when the marital bond is not yet fully realized through physical intimacy. The dissolution underscores the protective nature of the Hadd penalty in restoring the wife's honor and legal status.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of his companions who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘The man accuses his wife before he copulates with her. Heasws said: ‘He would be whipped the Penalty (Hadd), and there would be separation between him and her’.
